decision_inputs.attack_query: Can a bidder, seller, operator, or observer exploit ordering, partial information, deadlines, ties, cancellation, or inventory custody to extract or strand value?

bounded_model.bounds: asset list, bond schedule, fees, phase lengths, inventory authority, lot rules, and terminal thresholds remain unselected
exclusions: existing auction-custody balances do not prove funded inventory ingress

game_surface.authoritative_state: inventory custody, bond escrows, commitments, reveals, fills, payments, rounding, refunds, and slashes
game_surface.loss_surface: unfunded inventory, reveal theft, ordering manipulation, ambiguous cancellation, bond misallocation, or incomplete terminal drain

observed_research_behavior: Both seller-auction and two-party private-swap research lifecycles implement commit, reveal, settle, cancel, and expire phases with integer heights.
Seller settlement derives a uniform clearing price, uses deterministic pro-rata remainder ordering, refunds revealed bonds, and slashes non-reveals.
Seller inventory must already exist under an auction-derived ledger owner, while the command language does not select its deposit authority or fee owner.
Private settlement requires exactly two reciprocal full-amount reveals and refunds both bonds after atomic balance exchange.
